**Assessment**  
Mostly yes. In 2024 Marcos did convert several core declarations into visible implementation: new laws, executive orders, monitoring systems, agency suspensions, task-force reshuffles, and formal enforcement. The main limitation is that some flagship promises were only partially delivered, and some of the public framing remained branding-heavy or self-reported.

**Evidence For**
- [EO 52 institutionalizing and expanding Pag-Abot for street dwellers and other vulnerable individuals](https://lawphil.net/executive/execord/eo2024/eo_52_2024.html) | Lawphil / Office of the President | January 18, 2024 | Marcos turned a social-protection promise into a standing inter-agency program with monitoring and biannual reporting. | QIDs: 8B.6, 8B.5, 8B.3
- [PBBM adopts DICT’s National Cybersecurity Plan 2023-2028](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-adopts-dicts-national-cybersecurity-plan-2023-2028/) | Presidential Communications Office | April 6, 2024 | The government converted cybersecurity policy into a whole-of-nation roadmap requiring agencies and LGUs to implement and report. | QIDs: 8B.6, 8B.5, 8B.2
- [PBBM signs laws on streamlining procurement, combatting online scams](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-signs-laws-on-streamlining-procurement-combatting-online-scams/) | Presidential Communications Office | July 20, 2024 | Procurement promises became statute-backed rules, standardized forms, and e-procurement, which is observable administrative implementation. | QIDs: 8B.6, 8B.5, 8B.2, 8B.4
- [PBBM stands by suspension of 139 NFA officials](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-stands-by-suspension-of-139-nfa-officials/) | Presidential Communications Office | March 6, 2024 | Marcos backed disciplinary action against a large batch of officials over anomalous rice sales, showing enforcement rather than mere rhetoric. | QIDs: 8B.6, 8B.5, 8B.4
- [PBBM orders implementation of amnesty program to communist rebels](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-orders-implementation-of-amnesty-program-to-communist-rebels/) | Presidential Communications Office | April 4, 2024 | An announced amnesty became an implementation order with agencies told to finalize the IRR, a concrete execution step. | QIDs: 8B.6, 8B.5, 8B.3
- [PBBM orders activation of online platform to monitor El Niño-La Niña phenomena](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-orders-activation-of-online-platform-to-monitor-el-nino-la-nina-phenomena/) | Presidential Communications Office | March 26, 2024 | Marcos moved from climate-risk talk to a public dashboard with sector conditions, interventions, and citizen reporting. | QIDs: 8B.6, 8B.5
- [PBBM calls for comprehensive national flood-control plan to protect communities and production areas](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-calls-for-comprehensive-national-flood-control-plan-to-protect-communities-production-areas/) | Presidential Communications Office | July 26, 2024 | The administration translated disaster-response rhetoric into a named flood-control push and swift assistance after Typhoon Carina/Habagat. | QIDs: 8B.6, 8B.5, 8B.2
- [PBBM reorganizes inter-agency task force on zero hunger](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-reorganizes-inter-agency-task-force-on-zero-hunger/) | Presidential Communications Office | August 9, 2024 | Food-security goals were reworked through formal coordination machinery,

**8B.6 Research Note**

**Assessment:** Mostly yes, with clear partial-failure caveats. Marcos’s 2024 record shows repeated conversion of announcements into instruments, rules, and administrative actions. The weak point is that some flagship promises, especially rice affordability, had only partial or contested implementation, so not every declaration translated cleanly into outcomes.

**Evidence Against / Limits**

It shows the slogan and intended direction, but not delivery by itself. | QIDs: 8B.6, 8B.1
- [PBBM’s economic reforms improved lives in 2024](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbms-economic-reforms-improved-lives-in-2024/) | Presidential Communications Office | December 31, 2024 | The year-end wrapup is self-reporting and should be treated as weaker evidence than independent implementation records. | QIDs: 8B.6, 8B.1, 8B.2
